subject: SaaSCo renewal — phased GPU top-up + ephemeral overflow option
messages:
From: Alex Gomez <alex.gomez@saasco.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 28 Jul 2027 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal + capacity increase — exploring overflow approaches

Hi Logan,

We're getting close to our renewal window and want to lock in an expansion to our Dedicated pool. Current ask from engineering: add +40 GPUs (NVIDIA A100-equivalent) over the next quarter. Key constraints from our side:

- Need predictable throughput during business hours: target sustained 280 tokens/sec for our primary inference path.
- We expect several short spikes (5–20m) where throughput can double for sudden customer growth.
- Security requires any spillover to be in Redwood-managed capacity (we cannot route to third-party inference providers).

Questions:
1) Can Redwood commit to a phased provisioning schedule (e.g., +20 GPUs on day 0, +20 on month 2) with performance targets tied to each tranche?
2) For overflow, we'd prefer an "ephemeral overflow" model — i.e., on-demand spillover within Redwood's pool billed at a premium rate that automatically scales for short bursts, but with configurable safety limits. How does that compare to a hard cap approach?
3) What changes to contract terms do we need (term length, minimums) for reserved capacity + ephemeral overflow?

Would appreciate a one-page sketch and cost delta to review with procurement (cc'd).

Thanks,
Alex
Alex Gomez
VP of Infrastructure
SaaSCo

From: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>
To: Alex Gomez <alex.gomez@saasco.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 28 Jul 2027 17:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal + capacity increase — exploring overflow approaches

Alex — thanks for the clear ask. Looping in Karthik (SE) and Lauren (AM) so we can propose operational and contractual options. Quick answers up front, then a proposed plan.

Short answers:
- Phased provisioning: yes — we can stage the reserved pool in two tranches with performance guards at each delivery milestone.
- Ephemeral overflow: supported. We have an on-demand spill pool (Redwood-managed GPUs) that can be used for short bursts; it's billed at a premium per-token/second and comes with soft safeguards you can configure (e.g., max burst minutes per day, cost cap).
- Contract changes: we'll offer this as a renewal amendment (addendum) to the Dedicated agreement. Typical asks: 12–24 month term, committed baseline of reserved GPUs, and a defined premium rate for ephemeral overflow.

Proposed high-level plan (sketch):
1) Tranche 1 (day 0): +20 reserved GPUs provisioned and load-tested. SLO: 280 tokens/sec sustained across the reserved pool with p95 token latency < 200ms for your primary model.
2) Tranche 2 (month 2): +20 reserved GPUs added. Until tranche 2 is live, ephemeral overflow covers bursts beyond Tranche 1 capacity.
3) Ephemeral overflow behavior: on-demand Redwood-managed GPUs assigned automatically when reserved capacity is saturated. Overflow pricing = reserved unit price * 1.8 (example), with configurable caps:
   - daily burst minutes cap (default: 120m)
   - maximum concurrent overflow GPUs (default: 40)
   - an automatic throttle/fallback policy to maintain p99 latency targets if overflow becomes sustained
4) Contractual protections: optional credit/backstop if we exceed agreed tail-latency or fail to provision Tranche 2 on time.

Karthik — can you add notes on load-testing and the exact SLO measurement? Lauren — I'll follow up with a draft amendment and cost delta for Alex/procurement.

Cheers,
Logan
Logan Wright
Account Executive — Enterprise
Redwood Inference

From: Alex Gomez <alex.gomez@saasco.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@saasco.com
Date: Fri, 30 Jul 2027 09:23:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal + capacity increase — exploring overflow approaches

Logan — thanks. A few clarifying items from procurement and engineering:

- Procurement: we need a clear delta in monthly committed spend for the two tranches and the per-minute/per-GPU overflow math so we can map cost to budgets. Also please call out any minimum term changes (we prefer 12 months).
- Engineering: the SLO callout is helpful. For us, the most important guarantees are:
   1) sustained throughput target (280 tokens/sec) measured as a 10-min rolling average,
   2) p95 token latency < 200ms during business hours,
   3) burst margin: when overflow spins up, tail latency should not exceed p99 < 600ms for more than 2% of burst minutes.

One constraint: we do NOT want automatic fallback to a lower-quality quantized model during overflow without a pre-authorized policy. If overflow triggers a model variant with different output characteristics, that must be a manual escalation.

Can you produce a short amendment with: phased provisioning dates, firm pricing (tranches + overflow rates), configurable caps, and a DocuSign-ready signature block? We'll aim to sign within two weeks if numbers look good.

— Alex

From: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>
To: Alex Gomez <alex.gomez@saasco.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, procurement@saasco.com
Date: Sun, 01 Aug 2027 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal + capacity increase — exploring overflow approaches

Alex / team — attached is a concise amendment and a line-item cost delta (see Redwood_Dedicated_Proposal_SaaSCo_v2.pdf). Summary highlights below and next steps.

Summary (extracted):
- Term: 12 months (renewal amendment).
- Reserved capacity: +40 GPUs staged: 20 provisioned on signing, remaining 20 scheduled at day 60 (we include a 5-business-day buffer for provisioning).
- Pricing: committed GPU unit price = $X/month (see PDF). Ephemeral overflow rate = committed unit price * 1.85 when used in 15-minute windows. Overflow billing is per-minute rounded up.
- Caps you can configure in the console or via the amendment UI:
   • Daily burst minutes cap (default 120)
   • Max concurrent overflow GPUs (default 40)
   • Daily spend cap (customer-settable)
- SLOs: 10-min rolling avg throughput target = 280 tokens/sec (measured at the Redwood ingress). p95 token latency < 200ms business hours. Overflow tail allowance: p99 < 600ms for <= 2% of burst minutes; credit rules specified in section 4 of the amendment.
- Model quality fallback: explicit: no automatic fallback to alternative model variants during overflow unless pre-authorized. We will provide a policy toggle in the console and will not change model variants without your approval.
- Operational: Karthik will run acceptance load-tests on Tranche 1 after provisioning and provide the runbook for triggering overflow-grade scaling.

Next steps:
1) Review attached PDF and confirm any edits by Tue, 3 Aug.
2) We’ll generate a DocuSign amendment (link included) for signature once numbers are agreed — target ship: Wed, 4 Aug.
3) Tranche 1 provisioning within 5 business days of execution; Karthik to coordinate the load test slot.

Attachments: Redwood_Dedicated_Proposal_SaaSCo_v2.pdf (proposal + amendment draft). DocuSign link: https://www.docusign.com/redirect?doc=RDW-Amd-5342

If that timeline looks good I’ll have Lauren kick off formal pricing and the legal addendum.

Thanks — talk soon.
